notes:
I couldn't write these notes. The tool I use to search and read web pages gave an error saying I had no calls left. So I wasn't able to open any of the sources, including Enduring Word, the Bible Hub commentaries (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit), Wesley's Notes and Precept Austin.

You asked me to report only what the pages say, give a URL for every point and fill no gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, I have nothing I can back up. I haven't written any verse notes, because they would only come from memory.

When the tool works again, this is what I'd do:

1. **Verse-by-verse sources:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-33/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/33.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezekiel/33.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/ezekiel/33.htm
   - Wesley's Notes on Ezekiel at wesley.nnu.edu
   - Precept Austin's Ezekiel 33 page
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ**, I'd search for:
   - **Verse 11 ("I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked"):** how this fits with God choosing who is saved. I'd look for Reformed and Baptist views (desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, monergism.com) and Wesleyan views (seedbed.com, wesley.nnu.edu).
   - **Verses 12–13 and 18 (the righteous man who turns and dies):** whether a believer can lose salvation. I'd compare Calvinist teaching that true believers can't fall away (gty.org, ligonier.org, gotquestions.org) with Wesleyan/Arminian teaching (seedbed.com, Wesley's Notes). I'd also check Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org).
   - **Verses 7–9 (the watchman):** how the passage is applied to preachers and to evangelism today (spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, ag.org).
3. **Other views:**
   - The NET Bible notes (netbible.org) on the date in verse 21 and on the end of Ezekiel's muteness in verse 22.
   - Bible Odyssey (bibleodyssey.org) on the "Abraham was only one man" claim in verse 24.
   - Church Fathers' readings of verse 11 on newadvent.org, and catholic.com on repentance.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll fetch these pages and write the notes with a URL for each point.
